dedupe_keys.name: coastal resilience the nature conservancy web mapping tools and apps for coastal flood risk and nature based adaptation

description: Coastal Resilience is a programme led by The Nature Conservancy to examine the role of nature in reducing coastal flood risk. It combines an approach, a web mapping tool with a set of apps, and a network of practitioners supporting hazard mitigation and climate adaptation planning. The approach has four steps: assess hazard risk and community vulnerability, identify nature-based solutions, take conservation and restoration action, and measure effectiveness. Coverage: projects in 17 US coastal states, the Caribbean, Mexico and Central America, plus a global effort. Apps described on the site include a Resilient Coastal Cities app that visualises flood risk and adaptation options, tools for designing living shorelines, for marsh restoration, for sediment management and for fish habitat, and guidance on using nature-based solutions within the FEMA Community Rating System. Format and access: online mapping tool and apps; free to use. Licence (read on 2026-09-29): TNC terms of use: single copy for personal, non-commercial use. Simulation uses: flood exposure and adaptation scenarios for coastal communities and the roads, ports and utilities within them. Related records: the Global Value of Mangroves for Risk Reduction, another TNC dataset, is recorded on another round 2 branch; the NWRM platform (data-nwrm-natural-water-retention-measures-catalogue) covers nature-based water retention in Europe.
